In brief: the physical evidence (0.4 mm subsurface origin, crescent microcracks, white-etching cracks, butterfly microstructure, all cut through the active axial spall) is inconsistent with the operator's boundary-lubrication wear-through hypothesis, which is a surface-initiated mechanism and cannot explain a subsurface-initiated crack network. The verified failure mode is WEC-driven premature subsurface fatigue ("axial cracking"), a phenomenon independently documented by a dedicated multi-year DOE/NREL/GE/Flender/SKF research program investigating exactly this bearing class and position. Electrical bearing current is the leading candidate driver given this bearing's position adjacent to the converter-coupled generator, but it is not established to the exclusion of transient-load/sliding or inclusion-driven mechanisms; the cold-snap is, at most, a secondary accelerating input. Overall confidence is LOW (capped by the weakest contributing chains), though the core recommendation — do not authorize a same-spec replacement without completing a diagnostic package (independent re-metallurgy, SEM/EDM inspection, converter-current measurement, SCADA pull, hydrogen analysis) — is robust at MEDIUM confidence on its own.
